title: Krytical Nova - Volume 2 (Flow)
note: Volume 2, after the owner's Volume 1 picks. Main inspiration RJ Pasin and Dante Swan: djent and metal guitar over trap production (808s, hat rolls), epic and fun, no jazz. New takes are from Google Flow Music (Lyria 3.5); the Volume 1 takes you kept are here too (marked Kept), so the changes play with them.

slots.when: Starts on the logo glitch (red and cyan on the dark page) and loops under the owner's cover painting.
slots.ends: Pressing a key plays the Title outro; the theme fades out over 2 s.

slots.when: The moment the player presses a key on the title page and the comic page turns.
slots.ends: Rings out; the Selection theme fades in under its tail.

slots.when: Fades in 1.5 s after the title theme is gone and plays through faction select, character select and the creator. Keeps the title's epic mood (owner, Vol 1).
slots.ends: Fades out over 3 s when the world starts loading.

slots.when: Same tempo and key as the Selection theme (100 BPM, D minor). Hovering a faction's banner swells its coat over the bed (Hegemony, Null, Covenant).
slots.ends: Sinks back under the bed when the pointer leaves; the chosen faction's coat stays a little louder in the creator.

slots.when: The free truce town around the Central Plaza, walking about. Upbeat and fun (owner, Vol 1), still lighter than a fight.
slots.ends: Drops out on the next bar when a Callout starts.

slots.when: A Callout starts (PlayerCombatState.InCallout). The server's MusicConductor keeps the beat; a skill pressed within 90 ms of it hits 6 % harder.
slots.ends: Fades out over 2.5 s, 6 s after the last blow.

cues.tags: Instrumental only, no vocals, no lyrics, no voices of any kind. Video game faction and character select menu music that carries on from an epic title theme: cinematic djent meets trap, 100 BPM, D minor, 4/4. Mid intensity, heroic and confident, never jazz, never lo-fi, never cartoonish. Heavy palm-muted 7-string guitar chugs locked to the kick, deep 808 sub bass, crisp rolling trap hi-hats, hard snare on the backbeat, a wide cinematic synth pad, and a soaring clean tapped guitar melody on top. Steady and loopable with room for menus. About 2 minutes.

Instrumental only, no vocals, no lyrics, no voices of any kind. Glossy cyber djent for a sleek futuristic corporate faction, 100 BPM, D minor, 4/4: crystal clean tapped guitar leads over tight djent chugs, glassy synth arpeggios, deep 808 sub bass, gated snare, trap hi-hats, polished neon city, cold, precise and confident. No funk, no jazz. About 90 seconds.

Instrumental only, no vocals, no lyrics, no voices of any kind. Upbeat, fun, bright video game hub town music for a sunny plaza where heroes gather between fights, 110 BPM, F major, 4/4. Energetic melodic metal and pop-punk guitars with catchy tapped guitar hooks, bouncy trap drums, 808 bass, sparkling synth arps, heroic and playful, feel-good adventure. Not jazz, not lo-fi, not a city at night. Lighter than battle music. Loopable, about 2 minutes.

Instrumental only, no vocals, no lyrics, no voices of any kind. Video game duel battle music, 150 BPM, E minor, 4/4: driving punk rock meets big beat electronica meets djent and trap. Drop-tuned 8-string guitar chugs locked to a four-on-the-floor kick, hard backbeat snare on every bar, 808 drops, rolling trap hi-hats, glitch stutters, and a soaring tapped guitar hook recognisable in one bar. Anime final-boss energy, fun and huge, very clear steady beat to fight to. About 2 minutes.
